acorn_squash.note: Picked once the rind hardens in late summer and early autumn; keeps a couple of months, less than butternut.

apple.note: Picked from late summer to mid autumn; keeping varieties come out of cold store through winter and into spring.

apricot.note: A short early-summer stone fruit; the season lasts only a few weeks in each area, and New Zealand picks around Christmas.

artichoke.note: Mediterranean plants are cut from late autumn right through spring; Brittany and other oceanic areas pick in summer.

asian_pear.note: Nashi ripen on the tree from late summer and keep well in cold store into winter.

asparagus.note: Spears are cut for about eight weeks in spring, ending around midsummer in cooler areas; Peru's coastal desert crops mainly from September to December.

aubergine.note: A heat-loving crop: high summer into autumn in warm temperate zones, most of the year in the tropics; cool maritime growers keep it under glass.

avocado.note: Fruit holds on the tree for weeks; Mexican highlands crop all year, Mediterranean growers from late autumn to spring, New Zealand in spring and summer.

beetroot.note: A cool-season root: pulled from early summer to autumn in the north and kept in store into winter, grown from late autumn to spring in mild areas.

bell_pepper.note: Field peppers colour up from midsummer to the first frost; in hot dry areas they are a winter crop, in cool maritime ones a glasshouse crop.

bilberry.note: Wild Eurasian berry picked in northern forests and mountain heaths in high summer; not grown in the south.

bitter_melon.note: A warm-weather gourd: summer and the rains in monsoon Asia, high summer only where winters are cold.

black_grape.note: Table grapes ripen from late summer to mid autumn; Indian vineyards are pruned to crop in the dry winter.

blackberry.note: Summer fruit in the humid subtropics, a late-summer bramble harvest elsewhere; Mexican highlands supply most of the year.

blackcurrant.note: A cool-climate bush fruit picked over a few weeks in July and early August; it needs cold winters.

blood_orange.note: Needs cold winter nights to colour: Sicilian and Spanish fruit runs from December to about April, Chongqing's from January to March.

blueberry.note: Northern bushes crop in high summer and wild boreal berries in late summer; Mediterranean, desert and highland growers fill the cooler months.

borlotti_bean.note: Fresh pods are picked in late summer, or at the end of the rains in the Andes and Mexico, once the beans swell; dried borlotti keep all year.

broad_bean.note: Fresh pods are a spring crop in mild areas, an early-summer one further north, a winter one in hot deserts and a late rainy-season one in highlands.

broccoli.note: A cool-season head: grown through winter in mild and dry areas, summer to autumn where winters are hard.

brussels_sprouts.note: Picked from the stalk from autumn into winter, sweeter after light frost; Mexican highland fields supply the winter months.

burdock.note: East Asian root dug in autumn and early winter, then kept in cold store for months; a small early-summer young crop also exists.

butternut_squash.note: Cut once the skin hardens in late summer and autumn and cured to keep for months; the heat-tolerant vines crop all year in the wet tropics.

cabbage.note: A cool-season head: winter in mild and dry areas, summer to autumn further north, where hard white heads are stored.

calamansi.note: Philippine lime with its main flush after the rains, August to November; in Malaysia and Indonesia the trees fruit all year.

carrot.note: Pulled in summer and autumn in cool climates and stored into winter; a winter and spring crop in warm and dry areas.

cassava.note: Roots can stay in the ground and are dug all year near the equator; elsewhere the harvest falls in the dry or cool season.

cauliflower.note: A cool-season curd: winter in mild and monsoon areas, summer into autumn where winters are cold, and on into winter in Brittany and Cornwall.

celeriac.note: A northern European root lifted in autumn that keeps well in store and is eaten through winter.

celery.note: Field celery is cut from midsummer to autumn in the north and grown through the cool season in warmer areas.

chard.note: A hardy cut-and-come-again leaf: autumn to spring around the Mediterranean and in the Indian cool season, summer into autumn further north.

chayotte.note: A perennial vine that crops most of the year in tropical highlands; in warm temperate gardens the fruit comes in autumn.

cherry.note: A short early-summer fruit: May to July in the south, June to August in cool maritime areas, and around Christmas in Chile.

chicory.note: Bitter leaves and red radicchio are cut from autumn through winter; forced white chicons follow the same cold season.

chili_pepper.note: Fresh pods ripen from high summer to the first frost in temperate zones; in India and hot dry areas the main pick is the dry winter.

chinese_cabbage.note: Napa cabbage is mainly an autumn crop, cut in November in Korea and northern China for kimchi; cool maritime and northern summers let it be cut from July.

citron.note: Large thick-skinned citrus picked from early autumn into winter, chiefly in Calabria, Corsica and Israel.

clementine.note: Easy-peel citrus of the Mediterranean winter, picked from October to January and held briefly on the tree.

collard_greens.note: A cool-season leaf best after frost in the American South; in the tropics and highlands it is cut all year.

corn.note: Fresh sweetcorn is a high-summer crop in temperate zones, follows the rains in monsoon areas and highlands, and avoids midsummer heat in deserts.

courgette.note: Summer squash picked young from late spring to early autumn, through the rains in the highlands; in hot desert areas it is a winter crop.

cranberry.note: Bogs in cool northern regions are harvested from mid-September to November; the firm berries keep for weeks through the holidays.

cress.note: A cool-season leaf: best in spring and autumn where summers are mild, through the winter where they are hot; it bolts in heat.

cucumber.note: A frost-tender summer crop in temperate zones and highlands; hot dry climates grow it in spring and autumn, monsoon ones into the rains, the tropics all year.

curly_endive.note: Frisée is a cool-season field salad, cut from late summer through autumn in the north and through the mild winter around the Mediterranean.

daikon.note: A cool-season radish sown in late summer and lifted from autumn into winter; the roots keep for weeks in cold storage.

durian.note: Thai orchards fruit from April to July; Malaysia and Indonesia have a main midyear crop and a smaller one around the turn of the year.

edamame.note: Soybeans picked green in high summer, a July to September treat in Japan, Korea and China; lowland East Java grows them for export all year.

endive.note: Chicory roots lifted in autumn are forced in the dark, giving pale witloof heads from November to April.

fennel.note: Bulb fennel bolts in heat: a winter and spring crop around the Mediterranean, a late-summer and autumn one further north.

fig.note: Fresh figs ripen from July to September after a small June breba crop; Indian Deccan orchards pick from February to May. They do not keep.

fresh_garlic.note: Green and wet garlic is pulled in spring and early summer, weeks before the main crop is lifted and cured.

friggitello.note: A small sweet Italian frying pepper, grown mainly in southern Italy and picked green from June to September.

garlic.note: Bulbs are lifted in early summer and cured; dry garlic then keeps well into the following winter and spring.

grape.note: Table grapes ripen from late summer into autumn; hot dry regions start in early summer and Indian vineyards crop in late winter.

grapefruit.note: A winter citrus picked from autumn into spring in Florida, the Caribbean and the Mediterranean; the fruit holds on the tree, stretching the season.

green_bean.note: A frost-tender summer bean in temperate zones; desert and monsoon growers crop it through the cool months, highland farms all year.

green_bell_pepper.note: Picked unripe, so it comes a few weeks before red peppers; a summer field crop in temperate zones, a cool-season one in hot dry ones.

green_chili_pepper.note: Grown and picked green all year in the tropics; in temperate zones the field crop runs from midsummer until the first frost.

green_tomato.note: Unripe tomatoes are mostly the last fruit cleared before frost; in the US South they are also picked early in summer for frying.

guava.note: Flowers and fruits almost continuously near the equator; in India the sweet winter crop is prized over the rainy-season one.

habanero_chili.note: Needs a long hot season: picked all year in the wet tropics, in the dry season in Yucatan and the Caribbean, in late summer where summers are hot.

hass_avocado.note: Highland Mexico picks Hass all year; Spain and California mainly late winter to early summer, Peru, South Africa and Queensland in the southern winter.

horseradish.note: Roots are lifted after the first frosts in autumn and keep in cold storage through winter until spring.

hot_chili_peppers.note: Fresh chillies ripen from midsummer to the first frost in temperate fields; in the monsoon belt the main harvest falls in the cool dry season.

jackfruit.note: South and South-East Asia's monsoon belt picks jackfruit from late spring into the rains; near the equator trees bear through much of the year.

japanese_plum.note: Japanese plums ripen in early to midsummer, ahead of European plums; the ume used for pickling is picked green in June.

kale.note: A cold-hardy brassica cut from autumn through winter where the ground stays open, sweetest after frost; the East African highlands grow it all year.

kiwifruit.note: Picked hard in autumn and ripened from cold store through winter into spring; New Zealand and Chile harvest from March to June.

kohlrabi.note: A cool-season brassica: summer to autumn in central and northern Europe, spring and autumn in Mediterranean gardens, winter on the Indian plains.

leek.note: Leeks stand in the field from late summer through winter where the ground does not freeze; colder areas lift them in autumn.

lemon.note: The main crop is picked from autumn into spring and holds on the tree; Indian and Caribbean lemons crop with the rains, New Zealand ones in winter.

lettuce.note: Lettuce dislikes heat: a summer crop in cool climates and a winter-to-spring crop in Mediterranean, desert and subtropical fields.

lima_bean.note: Fresh limas are shelled from late-summer pods, a speciality of the American South; dried and frozen limas are sold all year.

lime.note: Limes bear all year in the wet tropics; Mexico and India peak with the summer rains, Brazil from January to June.

lingonberry.note: A wild berry of northern forests, gathered from late August into October; it keeps unusually well for a fresh berry.

lotus_root.note: Rhizomes are dug from the drained ponds from early autumn and through winter; they keep best left in the mud until needed.

mandarin.note: A winter citrus: clementines and satsumas from October or November, later mandarins into early spring.

mango.note: India and South-East Asia pick mangoes from the hot season into the rains; Pakistan and Egypt in summer; Brazil, Peru and Australia from spring to late summer.

mustard_greens.note: A cool-weather green that bolts in heat: winter in China, northern India and the US South, spring and autumn in cooler climates.

nectarine.note: A summer stone fruit, picked from June to September in Mediterranean orchards and in midsummer further north; New Zealand from December.

nettle.note: Young nettle tops are gathered in spring before the plants flower and turn coarse.

okra.note: A heat-loving pod picked young through the hot months; in the wet tropics it crops all year.

onion.note: Bulbs are lifted when the tops fall, cured, and eaten from store through the following winter; India lifts a spring and an autumn crop.

orange.note: Navels ripen from late autumn through winter; Valencia types follow and hang on the tree into late spring.

pak_choi.note: A quick cool-weather brassica that bolts in heat: spring and autumn crops in cold climates, winter where it is warm.

parsley_root.note: A central European root lifted in autumn and kept in cool storage for winter soups.

parsnip.note: Dug from autumn; frost sweetens the roots, which are left in the ground or stored into early spring.

passionfruit.note: Vines crop almost continuously in the humid tropics and highlands; in drier or cooler places fruit falls ripe in late summer and autumn.

pea.note: A cool-season pod: fresh peas come in spring around the Mediterranean, early summer further north, and the dry winter in India and the deserts.

peach.note: Tree-ripened peaches run from early summer varieties to late ones in September; they do not keep.

pear.note: Picked from late summer into autumn and ripened off the tree; winter pears are kept in cold stores for months.

pineapple.note: Induced flowering gives fruit all year in the wet tropics; elsewhere the natural crop ripens in the warm months.

plum.note: Early Japanese plums start in June in warm regions; European plums and damsons follow in late summer.

pomegranate.note: Ripens in autumn in dry warm climates and late summer in the Mexican highlands; the thick-skinned fruit keeps well for a couple of months.

potato.note: New potatoes come first, then the main crop is lifted in late summer and autumn and stored through winter.

prickly_pear.note: Cactus fruit ripens in summer in Mexico and the Middle East; Sicilian late crops run into November.

pumpkin.note: Harvested before frost in autumn, or at the end of the rains in the highlands, and cured; hard-skinned pumpkins keep through winter.

pumpkin_leaves.note: Tender leaves and shoots are picked while the vines grow, which in savanna regions and highlands means the rainy season.

purslane.note: A heat-loving summer annual, picked young through the warm months; in Mexico it is a rainy-season green.

quince.note: Ripens in autumn, later in cool oceanic gardens; the hard fruit keeps for a couple of months in a cool store.

radicchio.note: A cold-season chicory: Italian radicchio is cut from autumn through winter, when frost sharpens its colour.

radish.note: A quick cool-season root: winter in mild climates and on the Indian plains, spring and autumn where summers are hot, summer in cool ones.

rapini.note: Broccoli rabe bolts in heat, so it is cut in the cool months: autumn to early spring in southern Italy.

raspberry.note: Summer-fruiting canes crop in early summer and autumn varieties follow; Mexican highland fruit comes in winter.

red_bell_pepper.note: Red is the fully ripe stage, so field peppers turn red from midsummer into autumn; hot dry regions grow them in winter.

red_cabbage.note: Harvested from late summer to early winter and stored, so it is the classic cabbage of autumn and winter cooking.

red_chili_pepper.note: Chillies redden late in the warm season; Indian red chilli is a winter crop and Indonesian harvests peak in the dry season.

red_onion.note: Lifted when the tops fall in summer (spring in hot dry regions) and cured; red onions keep for several months.

redcurrant.note: A short midsummer berry from cool-climate gardens and farms, picked in strings over a few weeks.

rhubarb.note: Outdoor stalks are pulled from spring into early summer; the pink forced rhubarb of late winter is grown in dark sheds.

rocket.note: A cool-season leaf that turns hot and bolts in summer heat: spring and autumn in the south, summer in the north.

rose_hip.note: Wild hips are gathered in autumn once they turn deep red, ideally soft after the first cold nights.

roselle_flower.note: Roselle flowers as the days shorten; the fleshy calyces are picked from October to January, from Malaysia to the Caribbean, where they make Christmas sorrel.

russet_potatoes.note: Russets are a late main-crop potato dug in autumn and stored for most of the following year.

rutabaga.note: A hardy cool-climate root lifted from autumn into winter and kept in cellars until spring.

savoy_cabbage.note: Frost-hardy and sweeter after cold: cut from autumn right through winter where the ground does not freeze hard.

seedless_grape.note: Table grapes ripen from midsummer to autumn, earliest in hot deserts; India harvests in its dry late winter.

shallot.note: Bulbs are lifted in summer once the tops die back, or in the dry season in the tropics, and keep for months after curing.

snow_pea.note: A cool-season pod: spring in mild areas, early summer further north, the dry cool months in tropical highlands.

spinach.note: Bolts in heat, so it is a winter leaf in mild climates and a spring and autumn crop where summers are warm and winters hard.

spring_onion.note: Pulled young and green: spring in temperate areas, all summer in cool maritime ones, and the cool months in monsoon and humid subtropical climates.

strawberry.note: Field berries ripen in spring in mild areas and early summer in the north; warm deserts and highlands crop in winter.

sweet_onion.note: Mild high-sugar onions such as Vidalia are lifted in late spring and summer; they keep only a few weeks to months.

sweet_potato.note: Dug in autumn before frost and cured, then kept through winter; New Zealand kumara is dug from March to May. Grown and dug year round near the equator.

tangerine.note: A winter citrus that ripens from late autumn and holds on the tree for a few weeks after.

taro.note: Corms are dug as the leaves yellow at the end of the warm season, in Korea and northern China in September and October; harvested all year in the wet tropics.

taro_leaves.note: Young leaves are cut while the plant grows, so they follow the warm rainy season; year round in the wet tropics.

tomatillo.note: Mexico grows it all year in the central highlands; elsewhere it is a summer crop like tomatoes, and a winter one in hot lowlands.

tomato.note: Field tomatoes ripen from midsummer to early autumn; hot dry and monsoon areas grow the main crop in the cool season, the wet tropics all year.

turnip.note: Main-crop roots are lifted in autumn and early winter and keep in store for a few months.

water_spinach.note: Grows fast in hot wet weather: cut all year in the tropics and through the summer in southern China.

watercress.note: Spring-fed beds give the best cress in spring and again in autumn; it grows coarse and bitter in summer heat.

watermelon.note: Needs a long hot summer: high summer in warm temperate areas, the hot dry months before the monsoon in South Asia.

wax_bean.note: Yellow snap beans are picked young from midsummer to early autumn; in hot deserts they are a cool-season crop from November to April.

white_cabbage.note: Firm heads are cut from late summer to autumn in the north and kept in cold store through winter; a winter crop in mild areas.

white_onion.note: Bulbs are lifted when the tops fall in summer, or in spring in hot dry areas, then cured and stored for months.

yam.note: True yams are dug from the end of the rains, starting with new-yam festivals in West Africa, and keep for months.

yambean.note: Jicama roots are lifted in the dry season after a long warm growing period and keep for several weeks.

yardlong_beans.note: A heat-loving bean picked through the hot months; cropped all year in the humid tropics and in high summer in northern China.
